option_description: Controls whether egress firewall rules block workstations from sending DNS queries (UDP/TCP port 53) directly to arbitrary external resolvers, forcing all DNS traffic through designated internal resolver IPs only.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the 'permissive_dns_recursion_and_tunneling_path' exposure when this attribute is false AND dns_payload_inspection_enabled is false. Without this restriction, attackers can bypass internal DNS controls entirely by querying external resolvers directly, and can use DNS tunneling (e.g., iodine, dnscat2) as a covert exfiltration channel that circumvents egress filtering on ports 80/443.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On the perimeter or internal firewall (Cisco ASA, Palo Alto, iptables), query the egress ACL or security policy for rules covering port 53 from the workstation subnet. Look for permit rules scoped to internal resolver IPs and explicit deny-all for port 53 to any other destination.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACE entries showing 'permit udp <workstation-subnet> host <resolver-ip> eq 53' followed by 'deny udp <workstation-subnet> any eq 53'. If only a broad permit exists, the control is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a workstation in the zone, attempt to send a DNS query directly to a public resolver such as 8.8.8.8 using dig or nslookup. If the query succeeds and returns a result, the egress restriction is not enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A timed-out or connection-refused response confirms the restriction is in place. A valid DNS response indicates the firewall rule is missing or misapplied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the firewall management console (e.g., Palo Alto Panorama, Fortinet FortiManager, or Cisco FMC), navigate to the outbound security policy for the workstation zone and filter rules by destination port 53. Verify that only the internal resolver IPs are permitted as DNS destinations.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Palo Alto Panorama > Policies > Security > Filter by 'Application: dns' or 'Destination Port: 53' > Review destination zone/address for workstation-sourced rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A dedicated DNS egress rule explicitly naming internal resolver objects as the destination, with a subsequent deny rule covering any remaining port-53 traffic.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Linux-based firewall or router appliances, inspect the iptables or nftables ruleset exported from the running configuration. Look for OUTPUT or FORWARD chain rules governing port 53 from workstation subnet CIDRs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACCEPT entries scoped to the internal resolver IP for dpt:53, followed by DROP or REJECT entries for all other dpt:53 traffic from workstation CIDRs.

option_description: Identifies the authentication mechanism enforced on network switch ports in office common areas and conference rooms, selecting among 802.1X (dot1x), MAC-based admission control (mac_based), both simultaneously, or no authentication (none).
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the 'unmonitored_physical_network_access_points' exposure immediately when this value is 'none'. With no port authentication, any device physically plugged into a common-area jack joins the workstation zone without identity verification, enabling rogue device insertion, passive sniffing, and lateral movement from a position that inherits full intranet trust.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS switches, display the interface configuration for ports assigned to common-area or conference-room VLANs. Check for 'dot1x port-control' and 'mab' directives to determine which method, if any, is configured.
how_to_obtain.command: show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | include dot1x|mab|port-control
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'dot1x port-control auto' indicates 802.1X; 'mab' indicates MAC-based; both lines together indicate 'both'; absence of either indicates 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Aruba or HP ProCurve switches, check the authenticator port-access configuration for common-area ports to identify the active authentication mode.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output includes 'Auth Mode' showing '802.1X', 'MAC-Auth', or 'Mixed' (both). No authenticator entry or 'Disabled' indicates 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Cisco ISE or Aruba ClearPass, navigate to the network device or switch port inventory and filter by location tag corresponding to conference rooms or common areas. Review the assigned authorization policy to confirm whether dot1x or MAB is actively enforced versus monitoring-only.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cisco ISE > Administration > Network Resources > Network Devices > Select switch > View assigned policy sets; or ClearPass > Configuration > Network > Devices > Select switch > Policy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy set showing dot1x or MAB enforcement rules in 'Enforce' mode, not 'Monitor' mode. Absence of a matching policy confirms 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the network engineering team or review the network access policy documentation to confirm the intended authentication method for common-area ports and whether any exceptions have been granted for conference room infrastructure (e.g., VoIP phones or AV systems using MAB).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented policy specifying the authentication method per port type/location. Undocumented exceptions or verbal confirmation of 'nothing configured' indicate 'none'.

option_description: Counts the number of currently active (enabled, link-up or administratively enabled) switch ports in common areas or conference rooms that have neither 802.1X nor MAC-based admission control configured, representing the total exposure surface for unauthorized physical network access.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'unmonitored_physical_network_access_points' when this count is greater than zero AND nac_solution_deployed is false. Each unauthenticated port is an independent entry point into the workstation zone. Even a single uncontrolled port in a publicly accessible area such as a lobby or conference room is sufficient for an attacker to plug in a device, join the zone, and begin lateral movement without any authentication challenge.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS switches, enumerate all interfaces assigned to common-area VLANs that are administratively up and lack dot1x/mab configuration. Combine 'show interfaces status' output with 'show running-config' to cross-reference VLAN assignments against authentication settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of active ports. Cross-reference each against 'show run int <id> | include dot1x|mab'. Ports with no matching authentication directive are unauthenticated. Count those assigned to common-area VLANs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a Python script with Netmiko or NAPALM to iterate over all switches and collect port authentication state, then filter for common-area VLAN IDs and active ports lacking authentication configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: python3 -c "from netmiko import ConnectHandler; net_connect = ConnectHandler(device_type='cisco_ios', host='<switch-ip>', username='<user>', password='<pass>'); print(net_connect.send_command('show dot1x all summary'))"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of ports with dot1x status. Entries marked 'No' or absent from the table that are in common-area VLANs and currently connected are unauthenticated candidates.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the NAC platform API (e.g., Cisco ISE ERS API) to retrieve the list of switch ports and their authentication posture. Filter results for common-area location tags and count those with no enforced policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response listing network devices and associated port policies. Ports without an assigned authentication policy set are unauthenticated. Count those matching common-area location metadata.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the switch management platform (e.g., Cisco DNA Center, SolarWinds NTA, or Aruba AirWave), navigate to the port inventory view, filter by VLAN IDs corresponding to common areas and conference rooms, filter by status 'Connected' or 'Active', and count entries where the security column shows no authentication method.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cisco DNA Center > Provision > Inventory > Network Devices > Select Switch > View Device Details > Interfaces tab > Filter VLAN = <common-area-vlan-id>, Status = Connected
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A filtered list of connected ports in common-area VLANs. Each entry lacking a dot1x or MAB indicator in the security column increments the unauthenticated count.

option_description: Indicates whether a Network Access Control platform (such as Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, or PacketFence) is integrated with workstation zone switches covering common areas and is actively enforcing admission policies in enforcement mode, not merely monitoring.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'unmonitored_physical_network_access_points' when nac_solution_deployed is false AND unauthenticated_ports_count is greater than zero. Without an enforcing NAC solution, there is no central mechanism to challenge, quarantine, or block unauthorized devices that connect to zone ports, making all physical access points viable entry vectors regardless of switch-level configuration intent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Log into the candidate NAC platform administrative console (Cisco ISE, Aruba ClearPass, PacketFence) and verify that the policy enforcement mode for the relevant switch group is set to 'Enforce' rather than 'Monitor' or 'Audit'. Check that the switches covering common-area ports are listed as managed network devices.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cisco ISE > Policy > Policy Sets > Review active policy sets; Policy > Policy Elements > Results > Authorization > Confirm 'Active' enforcement status. Also: Administration > Network Resources > Network Devices > Verify switches are registered.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy sets active in enforcement mode with associated network devices listing all switches in the common-area scope. 'Monitor Mode' or empty device list indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a Cisco IOS switch, verify that the RADIUS server group referencing the NAC platform is configured and that dot1x system-auth-control is globally enabled, confirming the switch is actively communicating with the NAC solution for enforcement.
how_to_obtain.command: show aaa servers | include RADIUS; show dot1x system-auth-control
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'RADIUS server <NAC-IP> ... Requests: <non-zero>' confirms active communication. 'dot1x system-auth-control' showing 'Enabled' confirms enforcement is globally active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Cisco ISE ERS API or ClearPass REST API to confirm the platform is reachable and returning active session data for workstation zone switches, validating that enforcement is operational rather than configured but non-functional.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response with active session entries for endpoints authenticated through switches in the common-area scope. An empty session list despite connected ports indicates NAC is not enforcing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request from the network operations team the current NAC deployment scope documentation and confirm whether common-area and conference-room switch ports are explicitly included in the enforcement scope, as NAC deployments are frequently phased and common areas may be excluded.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented scope listing specific switch hostnames or port ranges included in NAC enforcement. Exclusion of common-area VLANs or a 'monitor-only' note for those segments indicates false.

option_description: Indicates whether network device management interfaces (switch SSH/SNMP/web management, router management ports, firewall management interfaces) are assigned to a dedicated management VLAN with an ID that does not overlap with any workstation or user VLAN, ensuring physical and logical separation of the management plane.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'management_plane_cohabitation' directly when this attribute is false, and also in combination when management_acl_restricts_workstation_subnets is also false. If management interfaces share a workstation VLAN, any compromised workstation can directly attempt authentication against switch SSH, SNMP, or web management interfaces without traversing any additional boundary, enabling network device takeover from a single endpoint compromise.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS switches, display the VLAN database and compare the management interface VLAN assignment against the VLANs used for workstation subnets. The management VLAN ID must not appear in any workstation subnet VLAN list.
how_to_obtain.command: show vlan brief; show interfaces vlan <mgmt-vlan-id>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'VLAN <mgmt-id> Management' shown in the VLAN table with an IP address in a dedicated management subnet. If the same VLAN ID appears in workstation DHCP scope documentation, isolation is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On each managed switch, display the running configuration for the management interface and confirm the VLAN assignment, then compare against the list of workstation VLAN IDs obtained from the VLAN database.
how_to_obtain.command: show running-config | include interface Vlan|ip address
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Separate 'interface Vlan<mgmt-id>' with a management-range IP address, distinct from any 'interface Vlan<workstation-id>' entries. Shared VLAN ID or IP address overlap indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the network device baseline configuration files stored in the configuration management repository (e.g., Rancid, Oxidized, or vendor NCM). Search for management interface VLAN assignments and cross-reference against the IPAM or DHCP records for workstation VLANs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management interface assigned to a VLAN with a non-overlapping subnet prefix compared to all workstation VLAN entries. Matching VLAN ID or subnet indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Cisco DNA Center or SolarWinds NCM, navigate to the device configuration view for each switch and examine the VLAN-to-interface mapping. Confirm the management VLAN is tagged as isolated and does not appear in the workstation VLAN set.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cisco DNA Center > Provision > Inventory > Select Device > Configuration tab > Search 'interface Vlan' entries > Compare VLAN IDs against IPAM workstation VLAN list
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A management VLAN entry with a dedicated IP range not present in workstation VLAN assignments. Presence of the management VLAN ID in workstation subnet records indicates false.

option_description: Controls whether ACLs or firewall rules on network device management interfaces explicitly deny traffic sourced from workstation subnet CIDR ranges to management ports such as SSH (22), SNMP (161), HTTPS management (443, 8080, 8443), ensuring workstations cannot directly reach the management plane even if VLAN isolation is incomplete.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'management_plane_cohabitation' when both oob_management_vlan_isolated is false AND this attribute is false, creating a compounding exposure. ACL-based restrictions serve as a defense-in-depth control when VLAN isolation cannot be achieved or has gaps. Without these ACLs, a workstation that can route to the management VLAN (e.g., via flat routing) can directly authenticate to switch management interfaces and reconfigure network infrastructure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Cisco IOS devices, display the access list applied to the VTY lines and management interface. Confirm that it contains explicit deny entries for workstation subnet CIDR ranges before any permit statement for management-authorized hosts.
how_to_obtain.command: show ip access-lists | include workstation-subnet-range; show line vty 0 4 | include access-class
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'deny tcp <workstation-cidr> any eq 22' or similar entries preceding permit entries for authorized management hosts. Absence of deny entries for workstation CIDRs indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the management interface ACL on the switch or boundary device for all management-plane ports. Test reachability from a workstation IP to the management interface on port 22 using a network sweep tool to validate enforcement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All ports shown as 'filtered' or 'closed' when sourced from a workstation IP. Any port showing 'open' confirms the ACL is absent or misapplied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect ACL definitions in archived switch configuration files for entries explicitly referencing workstation subnet prefixes as denied sources targeting management ports. Pay attention to ACL ordering, as a broad permit before the deny renders the deny ineffective.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACL entries in order: 'deny tcp <workstation-cidr> any eq 22', 'deny udp <workstation-cidr> any eq 161', followed by 'permit tcp <mgmt-host-cidr> any'. Absence of workstation-deny lines or a broad permit preceding them indicates false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the firewall management console (Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco FMC, Fortinet FortiManager), filter security policies by destination matching the management interface IPs or management VLAN subnet and source matching workstation VLAN CIDRs. Verify that deny rules exist before any permit rules for management-port traffic.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Palo Alto Panorama > Policies > Security > Filter Source Zone = workstation-zone, Destination Address = mgmt-subnet, Application = ssh/snmp/https > Verify Action = Deny appears before any Allow
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A deny policy entry for workstation-sourced traffic to management destinations on relevant ports. If no deny rule exists or the first matching rule is 'Allow', the ACL does not restrict workstation subnets.

option_description: Describes the actual network path over which out-of-band management traffic for switches and boundary devices travels, categorized as a fully dedicated isolated OOB plane, the same VLAN as workstations (shared), a partially separated arrangement where some devices use dedicated paths and others do not, or unknown when the path cannot be determined.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'management_plane_cohabitation' directly when this value is 'shared_workstation_vlan', representing the worst-case condition. Even 'partially_separated' may trigger the exposure if combined with false on oob_management_vlan_isolated. A shared management path means that east-west traffic from any compromised workstation can reach switch management interfaces at Layer 2 or Layer 3, enabling infrastructure-level compromise without traversing any enforced zone boundary.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Perform a traceroute from a test workstation to the management IP of a core switch. If the path resolves without leaving the workstation VLAN (same L2 domain or single L3 hop through the default gateway with no firewall traversal), the path is shared. If the trace hits a dedicated management router or firewall before reaching the device, the path is at minimum partially separated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A single hop (default gateway) resolving directly to the management interface indicates 'shared_workstation_vlan'. Multiple hops traversing a dedicated management network device indicates 'dedicated_oob_plane' or 'partially_separated'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On core switches, inspect the routing table and VLAN interface assignments to determine how management traffic flows. Identify whether the management interface IP is reachable through the workstation default gateway or through a separate routing domain.
how_to_obtain.command: show ip route <mgmt-subnet-cidr>; show interfaces vlan <mgmt-vlan-id> | include Internet address
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If the route to the management subnet is via the same next-hop as workstation default routing, the path is 'shared_workstation_vlan'. A distinct next-hop or VRF route indicates separation. Mixed results across devices indicate 'partially_separated'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the network architecture team and request the network diagram showing the out-of-band management plane topology. Confirm whether a dedicated management network (physical or VRF-separated) exists, which devices are connected to it, and whether common-area switches are included or excluded from the OOB plane scope.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A network diagram explicitly showing a dedicated management VLAN or physical OOB network with all switches connected indicates 'dedicated_oob_plane'. A diagram showing management traffic sharing workstation VLANs indicates 'shared_workstation_vlan'. Partial coverage indicates 'partially_separated'. No diagram or inability to confirm indicates 'unknown'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review VRF configurations or management network topology files in the network configuration repository. Look for VRF definitions dedicated to management (e.g., 'vrf management' or 'vrf Mgmt-vrf') and verify that all switch management interfaces are bound to the dedicated VRF rather than the global routing table shared with workstation VLANs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of 'ip vrf management' with management interfaces bound to that VRF, and workstation SVIs in the global table indicates 'dedicated_oob_plane'. Absence of VRF separation with management interfaces in the global routing table indicates 'shared_workstation_vlan' or 'partially_separated'.
